📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any major announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time.".

The Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

According to recent reports, so, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

In the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

The Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. A brand-latest, separate Golden Pursuit campaign will let you earn some Skyrim-centric goodies up until 2nd December, as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Game Awards has unveiled its nominees for 2026, as selected by a global jury of more than 160 media publications and creator outlets.

This year’s nominees are led by Grand Theft Auto VI with eight nominations, including Game of the Year and Best Game Direction, followed by CONTROL Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem each with six nominations, and Phantom Blade Zero with five nominations.

Owners can vote now in all categories via authenticated online voting on official website. Voting will end on December 9 at 6:00 p.m. PT / 9:00 p.m. ET.

Recent findings suggest that the Game Awards 2026 will air live on December 10 from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California with awards, world premiere announcements and trailers, musical performances by The Game Awards Orchestra led by conductor Lorne Balfe, and other surprises. It will be viewable across more than 40 digital video platforms including Disney+, Live TV on PS5, Prime Video, Roblox, Steam, TikTok Live, Twitch, Twitter, YouTube, and many more.

Get the full list of nominees below.

Recognizing a game that delivers the absolute best experience across all creative and technical fields.

For outstanding storytelling and narrative development in a game.

Recognizing a game for outstanding community support, transparency and responsiveness, inclusive of social media activity and game updates / patches.

For outstanding creative and technical achievement in a game made outside the traditional publisher system.

For the best debut game created by a newly introduced independent studio.

For the best game playable on a mobile device.

Best Virtual Reality / Augmented Reality.

For the best game experience playable in virtual or augmented reality, irrespective of platform.

For the best game in the action genre focused primarily on combat.

For the best action / adventure game, combining combat with traversal and puzzle solving.

For the best game designed with rich player character customization and progression, including massively multiplayer experiences.

For the best game designed primarily around head-to-head combat.

For the best game appropriate for family play, irrespective of genre or platform.

Best game focused on real time or turn-based simulation or strategy gameplay, irrespective of platform.

For the best traditional and non-traditional sports and racing game.

For outstanding online multiplayer gameplay and design, including co-op and massively multiplayer experiences, irrespective of game genre or platform.

A massive part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Newly introduced Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

Industry observers note that in any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

Recent findings suggest that overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

Just in case you wanted a break from the GTA news, we thought we'd remind you that we've got a few games either releasing or being added to Xbox Game Pass today, and there's some interesting stuff in the mix here.

Sources indicate that the one that catches the eye is Vice: Magic City Mayhem, which we mentioned recently in our article about two Vice City games releasing in mid-November. While the cover art is very GTA-inspired, and it's set in a world with a "Vice City theme", it actually appears to have more in common with classic Zelda in terms of the gameplay style.

It's also a very temporary Xbox and and Epic Games Store exclusive, as the Steam, PS5 and Nintendo Switch versions have been slightly delayed for whatever reason.

Beyond this, three games are being added to the Xbox Game Pass Premium service today, with High on Life 2 arguably being the highlight (if you enjoy the kind of humour it throws at you). The other two are Call of the Elder Gods and Roadside Research, which are both worth a play as well.

GTA 6 is technically already out in some countries as well (such as Upcoming Zealand), but its official release date is November 19th rather than the 18th, so we'll highlight it in tomorrow's article instead.

We'll throw all of today's new Xbox releases and Xbox Game Pass additions down below.

Vice: Magic City Mayhem is a top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme. Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

Turn-based management roguelike. Command the Inquisition and rule an industrial city on the empire’s edge. Use your train to meet prisoner shipment quotas by hunting heretics and slaying magical beasts. Produce supplies, contain revolt, and sacrifice prisoners to stop the madness.

In a recent development, an intergalactic conspiracy threatens the fate of humanity! Team up with a wide cast of talking alien guns as you shoot, stab, and skate your way through the exotic locales to take down the bad guys and save your favorite species (humans)!

Journey to the far corners of the Earth and unearth ancient horrors in this Lovecraftian narrative puzzle adventure and sequel to 2020’s critically acclaimed Call of the Sea.

According to recent reports, roadside Research is a 1 to 4 player co-op gas station simulator. Except you’re aliens. And undercover. Do very human things like restocking shelves while preparing for the invasion. Just don’t get caught.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.

The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a fresh group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

Recent findings suggest that "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler mentioned in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the company swallowed up countless substantial names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

It doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has remarked it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Big Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The initial reviews have arrived for GTA 6, and it's safe to say the game has been an absolute smash hit with critics.

In a recent development, the metascore has settled on a 99, making it one point off a "perfect" score of 100. In a year stuffed with fantastic games massive and small, it's become the highest rated title of 2026.

More than that, though, it's the highest rated game of all time.

Reaching 99 is almost unheard of; only one other game has achieved the same level of acclaim — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998).

According to recent reports, however, GTA 6 has held onto its 99 score after more than 160 reviews; Ocarina of Time's metascore counts just 22 — though that's of course indicative of the era in which it released. There are simply more gaming outlets now, but that just means it's tougher to get consistent scores.

Rockstar's crime caper has received insanely consistent acclaim, and that might just give it an edge over the Nintendo classic. It's incredibly rare to see near-total agreement on a subjective work like this.

Critics are unanimous in their praise of GTA 6's open world, the relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia, and the complex systems behind its myriad characters, activities, and missions.

Here are some snippets from just a few of the reviews — including our own, of course.

Industry observers note that "GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.".

"Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.".

It has been revealed that "Like all videogame protagonists, Jason and Lucia are ciphers through which the player exerts their will on the digital world. And yet, through the co-authored interplay of the characters Rockstar has written, and the people you personally tune them into becoming, they form one of the great partnerships in entertainment: beautiful and deadly, open to the possibilities of their world and, despite the violence they inflict on those beyond their circle, driven forward not by fear, but by love.".

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content.".

Industry observers note that "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

"Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realising such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is a modern masterpiece. Rockstar's developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched. Minor performance concerns don’t dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait.".

Are you excited to hop into GTA 6 after reading all these glowing reviews? Tell us in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when everything's gone sideways at 3000ft you're going to need a parachute in GTA 6. Skyscraper diving is actually what got me into playing GTA 4 online with my friends so I'm definitely buckling in for some high altitude gliding in GTA 6. Here's how to sail the skies in Leonida.

Hop out of a plane mid-air or off the top of a building and while you're in freefall press the button prompt on screen to pull your chute and float to the ground. You can steer left and right, and angle yourself downward to descend more quickly or pull back to descend more slowly.

Sources indicate that you only need to buy a parachute one time, but you may need to reset it between uses. Head to a gun store and select it from the rack to add it back to your inventory before you go skydiving again. You can also just re-equip a parachute that you find on top of a skyscraper.

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a newly introduced dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big newly introduced lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

It has been revealed that if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

Industry observers note that there's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as massive a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

I've been especially curious about the future of The Penguin (which is streaming with a HBO Max subscription), and now we have an idea about what's going on behind the scenes.

Industry observers note that the Penguin is a spinoff of The Batman, and became an Emmy-winning hit after it arrived on HBO. The TV series made me way more invested in Matt Reeves' franchise, and I desperately want a sophomore season to be green lit. During Deadline's recent report about where things stand at DC, it claims that The Penguin showrunner Lauren LeFranc is "in talks" to produce a Poison Ivy series. Unfortunately, the studio is focused on The Batman: Part II before it can strategy any potential return to The Penguin.

In a recent development, the Batman: Part II is in the midst of filming, following delays and Matt Reeves' departure due to a family issue. Amidst leadership shakeups, the studio is seemingly focused on getting that title in the can. Fingers crossed that we we get more of The Penguin whenever that movie is finally completed.

The idea of Lauren LeFranc producing a Poison Ivy TV series is a thrilling one, although that developing project isn't set within the Matt Reeves Batman universe. I'll be sat if/when that show comes to life, but I also really need to see more of The Penguin, particularly Cristin Milioti's Sofia Falcone/ The Hangman.

Sofia was one of the main protagonists of The Penguin, and the actress' performance was incredible and earned her an Emmy Award. Unfortunately, Milioti won't be part of The Batman: Part II, despite her popularity among fans. What's more, Colin Farrell claimed he's only in two scenes of the forthcoming sequel. So why not put Cobblepot and Falcone center stage for a second installment of the acclaimed HBO series?

Right now there are countless questions about upcoming DC movies, and what's coming next for the burgeoning DC Universe. We're currently only a few installments into the original looks for Gunn's first slate of projects, titled Gods and Monsters. His replacement Jeremy Latcham is expected to start his run as the new CEO of the studio on December 1st, so maybe we'll get more information then.

Recent findings suggest that as of now, The Batman: Part II is expected to arrive in theaters on February 18th, 2028. If we have to wait that long before getting more news about The Penguin's future, fans like me are going to have to continue practicing patience. Give us more of Sofia Falcone, you cowards!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the Shadow of the King of Light, History is Written by the Survivors.
  • In Westalia, renown is more than just a story—it is a weapon of mass destruction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that calame, a single-player isometric strategy RPG that “blends deep, classic strategy with innovative reality-shifting gameplay,” will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam in February 2027, developer Nextale Games unveiled. A demo is right now available for PC.

Here is an overview of the game, via Nextale:.

In the Shadow of the King of Light, History is Written by the Survivors.

In Westalia, renown is more than just a story—it is a weapon of mass destruction. When belief in a legend grows strong enough, it can physically reshape the battlefield or devour those who wield it. To overthrow the tyrannical King of Light, the Rebellion must learn to harness this divine force without becoming the very monsters they fight. But how do you save a kingdom when you are tearing yourselves apart?

It has been revealed that an uneasy alliance forms the core of the Rebellion. On one side, Kenmare fights for the freedom of the people; on the other, the Panthers fight to reclaim the throne. While their alliance is a matter of sheer survival, their visions for the future are utterly irreconcilable—and you are the one chosen to lead them.

A New Kind of Tactics That Rewrites the Battlefield Itself.

Industry observers note that in the finest tradition of genre classics, Calame delivers demanding, handcrafted, grid-based combat where positioning, unit facing and class synergies are the keys to survival. Players can customize their army utilizing a diverse roster of melee specialists, ranged fighters, mages and support classes to trigger devastating party combinations.

However, Calame breaks the tactical mold with its groundbreaking “Correction” feature—an innovative newly introduced strategy mechanic allowing you to rewrite and manipulate the battlefield mid-combat, turning the terrain itself into a dynamic weapon!

Recent findings suggest that beyond the battlefield, Calame features deep progression systems including RPG leveling, skill unlocks, and legendary gear collection. Your journey is heavily defined by a reactive choice system. Decisions made at camp and during narrative events directly alter the Rebellion’s political alignment, unlocking powerful passive traits that permanently reshape your squad’s playstyle, faction relationships and the unfolding story.

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

In a recent development, "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a latest interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

Recent findings suggest that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.

Reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku says, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly," Gigliotti reportedly told staff. "There is no truth to these claims.".

In a recent development, this follows a recent rumour that the action adventure title was potentially going to get the axe in the near future. The rumour originated from a Marvel 1943 fan account, and while the original X post has since been deleted, it didn't stop it from spreading online, including amongst the game's own development staff.

According to Kotaku's report, Rise of Hydra is close to its alpha state, despite seemingly five years of development. The game is mentioned to have had multiple concerns through its long development.

The current build is reportedly "light on gameplay", featuring only one interaction button. This is understood to be the result of Rise of Hydra having reportedly been originally envisioned as a Netflix game. According to the same report, the game is late and over budget, which resulted in cuts to its scope and scale throughout development.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was fully revealed in 2024, and is the debut title of Skydance New Media, the studio headed by veteran designer and writer Amy Hennig, who's famed for her work on the Uncharted series of games.

It has been revealed that though the game was originally planned for release in late 2025, it was later delayed to early 2026 and then again to "beyond early 2026". Earlier this summer, Paramount Games Studio boss Shawn Kittelsen noted Rise of Hydra won't be out in 2026, but assured fans it remains in development. According to the report, Rise of Hydra was later delayed to 2027 and beyond.

Tensions are particularly high at the moment following the colossal recent Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, which has already resulted in some job losses at Paramount Games, a group that oversees the game's development, among other projects.

Furries are outlawed in GTA 6's fictional state of Leonida, but that won't stop you from breaking the law and helping them run from the cops if you so choose. This is GTA, after all.

Grand Theft Auto's satire has always been pretty all encompassing, taking aim at all corners of life under capitalist America. This time, GTA 6 also covers society's more extreme reaction to fringe groups like furries as a Leonida governor, Mike Jimenez, put an outright ban on the group before the events of the story, per the in-game social media app and news channels.

It has been revealed that en GTA VI, el gobierno permite que los cazadores maten a los furros. Además, se prohibió cualquier expresión suya, como el «UwU». Este odio los llevó a crear un culto secreto llamado «The Furverts». https://t.co/0huyel42eHNovember 18, 2026.

According to recent reports, "Governor declares Leonida furry-free," is one of the many headlines you can find while doomscrolling through Lucia and Jason's phones. In typical GTA fashion, the ban stemmed from wild political fears around a so-called "woke plague" and how it might impact the population of workers, apparently leading to an underground group of "Furverts.".

"It was bad enough seeing them in the park, but then we got porn sites using algorithms to turn honest working men into furries," the governor stated in an in-game statement. "That's why there had to be protection from this woke plague.".

A TV ad paid for by the Anti-Furry Association also warns folks to watch out for any suspected furry activity, gives licensed hunters permission to shoot people in fursuits and tells them to watch out for any animals using internet lingo like "Uwu," "Rawr" and "Hewwo.".

But in a series famous for its criminal exploits, you can of course decide to spit in the face of the discriminatory law. CNET's David Lumb reports that you can even help a persecuted furry escape the cops, link up with a litter of other furries, and then help them reach a secure compound. I'm sure in a game as big and winding as GTA 6, there's probably a ton more to discover about the group.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 takes more than a few jabs at politicians, even aside from the anti-furry law. Other headlines scattered across the game show some governors outright dismissing climate change concerns, for example, describing it as Earth's version of puberty. One even argues global warming is a good thing, actually, because it'll give office workers an excuse to dress "hotter." Good old Rockstar, eh?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad.
  • To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

According to recent reports, the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being mentioned, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just released into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

Recent findings suggest that that's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

Nvidia's board of directors has reportedly met to decide whether to remove the firm's embattled CEO Jensen Huang, as news of a second extramarital affair has come to light.

The board's decision has yet to be made, but there are three expected outcomes. Either Huang stays with the manufacturer and continues as Nvidia leader, despite the controversy or he is replaced as CEO, or he quits. Nvidia's share price dropped following reports of this meeting taking place.

Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it to become one of the world's most valuable companies - it interchangeably wears that crown, alternating with Apple. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'd better get used to seeing GTA 6 break records, because the game's not even out yet in most countries and it's already crushing long-standing numbers.

Indeed, the hype is so colossal that Rockstar's open worlder broke the all-time record for livestream viewers just minutes after its release in regions where it's already the 19th November.

According to Streams Charts' data, GTA 6 has peaked a frankly absurd 7.2 million viewers across streaming platforms Twitch (3.1 million), YouTube (2.7 million), and Kick (1.4 million), and others.

The crazy part is that this figure could well be eclipsed as GTA 6 becomes available in more regions, and more streamers start to broadcast their gameplay.

Team-based shooter Valorant previously held the all-time record, which was set back in 2020, when watching livestreams could net you access to the game's PC beta.

It peaked at 1.7 million viewers, meaning that GTA 6 has absolutely demolished the record — and honestly, it's hard to imagine anything topping it for years and years to come.

Have you contributed to any of these numbers by watching someone else play GTA 6? Or are you saving the experience for your own playthrough? Try not to spoil yourself in the comments section below.

[source streamscharts.com, via eurogamer.net].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a bit of a drive (or boat, or flight) to get all the way out to the Mile Zero military base on the big bridges to the southern keys but it's actually not that far away from the first house you've got access to at the start of the game in Key Lento.

You'll get a wanted level if you get spotted on base (and wind up in a pretty immediate gunfight for it) but this is still the easiest way to steal a tank or get your hands on a combat jet.

Mile Zero Air Station Southeast.

The easiest way to get into the military base without a full gunfight is to use the stunt jump Mile Zero Air Station Southeast. The name states it all: this jump is on the southeast corner of the base along the southern access road. You'll have to weave through a few slightly-manned concrete barricade checkpoints and take a bit of gunfire to reach it where there's a major dirt mound leading to the barbed wire fence around the base. Take your vehicle over that at speed to get credit for the stunt jump and land yourself inside the base.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets is arguably one of the best Paramount+ shows, although it required fans to get a Paramount+ subscription including Showtime. I'm personally a hardcore fan who is hyped about the fourth and final season's premiere this month. Folks are hoping to have Yellowjackets' biggest mysteries solved before it ends its run, and hopefully joins the ranks of TV shows that actually ended well. We know that the series guards it secrets from the public, but it turns out that even the cast is left in the dark about spoilers.

According to recent reports, yellowjackets' cast is an incredible multi-generational ensemble who tell the story across two timelines. The pressure is on for the Emmy-nominated series to stick the landing, and provide answers about various long-standing mysteries. In a recent interview with ScreenRant, Teen Shauna actress Sophie Nélisse was asked if she knew her character's fate ahead of time, to which she said:.

According to recent reports, no, we actually don't get the scripts more than like a week in advance, which is kind of fun because on set we're all sort of plotting and trying to reflect on what we have. We were coming up with our own theories of what the finale was going to look like, but we had no idea how they were going to get rescued, how their time in the wilderness would end. I obviously knew that Shauna was going to get married because we saw that.

In a recent development, well, my mind is blown. While Yellowjackets fans are being kept away from spoilers, I had no idea how tight the security was for even the cast. They only got each newly introduced script a week in advance, so Nélisse and her costars weren't able to use the full arc of their character to inform each performance. Instead they had to take things episode by episode and play each moment with honesty without looking ahead.

Fans have lingering questions about the No Eyed Man as well as the mystery involving Crystal's dead body. While we're still in the dark for now, so was the cast. The Heated Rivalry actress went on to say:.

Industry observers note that we just kind of went day by day with it. We were just always so excited when we got a new script because, as the audience feels when they finish an episode, it always kind of leaves us on a cliffhanger. That's how, whenever we read a script, we'd all message in the group chat, being like, ‘Oh, this one is so good! I love this bit, and I love that bit.’.

Celebrities: sometimes they really are just like us. Despite being the actors bringing Yellowjackets to life, they were left with episode cliffhangers in the midst of shooting Season 4. I have to wonder if Sophie Nélisse and her co-stars even know all the twists that are coming with the show's final season on the air.

In a recent development, yellowjackets Season 4 will premiere on November 20th as part of the 2026 TV schedule. The pressure is on for the drama series to stick the landing, but it looks like we'll get plenty of surprises in the final set of episodes.

That means Loki might not really be present for that moment, though we'll just have to wait and see.

Now, it could be that I just close the door and walk away. You be the judge. Every possibility remains open in a multiverse. But even if you knew nothing about what happens next, it's already a thrilling prospect. What on Earth are they going to say to each other? How is this going to go?".

It has been revealed that of course, the last time Steve Rogers saw Loki was during the events of The Avengers (and Steve briefly revisited this point of the Marvel timeline during the Endgame Time Heist). Breaking: Guide: GTA 6: Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1430 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know.
  • Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.
  • GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know. This spoiler-free GTA 6 guide includes info on a dozen key features and mechanics that will help you make the best start to your life in Vice City.

Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.

GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.

Press Options and select Settings > Gameplay. Scroll to the bottom (options 24 and 25) and you can choose to enable Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, as shown:.

Accessible Combat will both reduce the damage you take in gunfights, while increasing the damage enemies receive, making firefights much more manageable.

Reduced Vehicle Damage, meanwhile, will reduce the damage your car takes when in crashes or combat. This means there's less chance of your car becoming difficult to control or exploding.

The game will warn you that enabling these "changes the balance and experience of gameplay", meaning your experience will be a lot easier. Using them does not alter the story or disable Trophies, however.

GTA 6 has a upcoming control scheme which modernises its gameplay by mapping run to L3 and jump to Cross/X.

For those of you who've spent over a decade playing GTA 5 and GTA Online, however, you may prefer to use Rockstar's more traditional control scheme.

Fortunately, this is relatively easy to enable.

Press Options and select Settings > Control Scheme, as pictured:.

The control scheme will automatically be set to the latest Default layout, but you can toggle to Classic if you prefer the GTA 5 approach.

As its name implies, GTA 6 is all about grand theft auto — or, in other words, stealing cars.

Most vehicles you find parked around Vice City will be locked, but it is possible to steal them quicker with a very simple tip.

When the minigame for any criminal activities appear — like using your Slim Jim, Clone Key, or even hotwiring a car — there's a pink "sweet spot" you can find to speed up the action:.

This makes it quicker to break in and make a quick getaway.

Just move the sticks around to find the right spot, and use those extra seconds wisely to escape swiftly:.

GTA 6 has a living, breathing open world that encourages exploration. If you take the time to look around, you'll almost certainly discover something to do.

However, if you want to continue with the story and you're not sure what to do next, there's a way to easily see your next objective or story mission.

Press the Touch Pad to open your map and then using the index on the left of the screen, press Right to see a list of available story missions, with mandatory objectives at the top and optional ones listed below:.

You can immediately set a waypoint to any mission with Cross/X.

There is no traditional fast travel in GTA 6, but there is a way you can get around the map promptly for a nominal fee.

Bring up your smartphone by pressing Up and select RydeMe:.

You'll need to have an active waypoint, which you can choose from within the app or by picking one in advance via your map with Touch Pad.

You'll be notified a driver is on the way and you'll be able to see them from your minimap:.

Recent findings suggest that once you get in your Ryde, hold L2 to focus on your driver. You can then hold Triangle to skip your journey for $100 and immediately arrive at your destination:.

Longer journeys will cost more than shorter ones, but fast travelling this way is relatively inexpensive overall.

There are two types of money in GTA 6: cash stored in your wallet and money protected in your BuckMe bank. The latter will unlock as part of Chapter 1.

You can see both types of money at any time by pushing Down:.

Money stored in your wallet will be lost if you're Busted or Wasted during gameplay, so it's really vital you put this in your BuckMe bank.

The easiest way to do this is press Up to access your smartphone and select BuckMe > ATM Finder:.

This will automatically select a waypoint to the nearest ATM machine. Follow it and deposit any funds in your wallet into your BuckMe bank, where it'll be safe even if you get arrested or die:.

Throughout GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will build a criminal profile which can affect how NPCs and the wider world of Leonida responds to you.

Recent findings suggest that murdering enemies will contribute towards a more aggressive criminal profile. As such, you may want to consider a non-lethal approach.

One way to do this is by favouring stealth and grabbing enemies with R2, so you can cleanly knock them out without killing them:.

Another option, if you get caught up in a gunfight, is to target non-vitals like kneecaps and arms.

You can easily see non-vitals by pressing L3 and R3 and aiming at yellow parts of the body:.

You'll know an enemy has been debilitated without killing them if a yellow X appears in your weapon's reticule. A red X will appear if your target has been murdered.

If you need to set a quick waypoint to an notable location in GTA 6, you don't necessarily need to press Touch Pad to bring up your map.

Instead, hold Down and you'll get an alternative in-game view of any nearby shops, waypoints, or story missions:.

You can highlight any of these and press R3 to automatically set a GPS route to where you want to go.

There'll be times in GTA 6 when you're separated from your car and you want to spawn it nearby.

You can do this by opening your smartphone with Up and selecting the Scooter Bros app:.

Select which car you want to use from the app and you'll be charged a fee depending on the delivery distance and your car's current condition:.

Your car will then automatically spawn in a nearby location, marked on your minimap:.

Stealing or entering a car in GTA 6 does not mean you'll have access to it forever.

You'll need to park it in a Parking Space or Garage to temporarily store it, and register it at a Pay 'N' Spray to keep it forever.

Find a car you want to keep and set a waypoint for a Pay 'N' Spray, like with this Emperor Sultan I just stole:.

Sources indicate that drive into the Pay 'N' Spray and select Register to swap the plates. The fee commanded will depend on the value of the car:.

Sources indicate that note that you will need free Stored Vehicle slots to register your car. You can sell previous cars directly at the Pay 'N' Spray:.

Alternatively, you can press Up to open your smartphone and select Vice City Real Estate. This will let you buy more garages for additional Parking Spots:.

This feature becomes available during a story mission, so you may not immediately have access to it if you're still early in the campaign.

Generic upgrades are available for all vehicles at any Mod Shop, but if you want specialist tunings you need to go to the right shop.

These are marked with a blue Wrench icon.

Press Up to open your map and then Right to open the map index.

Select Vehicles > Mod Shops and look for a Mod Shop with a blue Wrench icon, as shown:.

Set a waypoint for the appropriate Mod Shop and you'll find all of the customisations and specialised upgrades available for your current vehicle.

Just like in real-life, staying on top of your smartphone notifications in GTA 6 can be time consuming.

Fortunately, the game will mark vital messages for you in the Reminders tab:.

Press Up to bring up your smartphone and then press Square to access your Reminders.

Here you'll find a curated list of key messages, including in-game news articles and NPCs who are waiting for your replies:.

Hopefully you've learned a thing or two with this spoiler-free GTA 6 walkthrough and collectibles guide. Are there any other tips and tricks you think the world should know? Share them in the comments section below.

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

In a recent development, first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

Sources indicate that I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

It has been revealed that the other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only confirmed this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then rapidly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

This is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when tech giant co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and Upcoming York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

Sources indicate that while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij stated. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the last time I saw Jared Padalecki, he was – here come some The Boys spoilers – brutally running through and killing people as Mister Marathon. The next time I saw him, he was playing an actor in a wholesome Netflix rom-com on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Talk about range. Seriously, I don’t think you can get something more different from a holiday romance than The Boys. So, when I spoke to Padalecki about his fresh rom-com, Guarding Stars, I asked what it was like jumping between the two projects.

Sources indicate that when I was chatting with Padalecki about his book-to-screen adaptation of Katherine Center’s rom-com The Bodyguard, I also mentioned that the last time I saw him was for the Supernatural reunion on The Boys. He immediately cut in to say that the two projects are “very different,” and when I asked him what it was like to jump from one to the other, he explained:.

In a recent development, that is weird. It was weird. It was also weird jumping into The Boys in the first place. You know, I'd seen every episode of the show that was out, but I knew I'd be there with [Eric] Kripke and Phil Sgriccia and [Jensen] Ackles and Misha [Collins]. So that was fun.

What’s funny is Jensen Ackles also described this reunion as “weird.” Anyway, getting to Padalecki’s comments, he told me that when it came to The Boys, he wasn’t exactly telling his parents or children to use their Amazon Prime subscription to see it. It was gory and wild, so yeah, that left him saying:.

It was one of those things also where I was like telling my mom and dad like, ‘Maybe don't watch this yet’ or like ‘Maybe don't watch it with any people under the age of 21 or 18 or whatever.’ But it was fun.

Well, considering this reunion was called “one of the most fun and bloodiest hours in all of 2026 TV,” I can see why Padalecki wasn’t exactly recommending it to children. However, he had a blast, and when it came time to flip the switch from blood, gore and grossness to wholesome Christmas and romance, it wasn’t a problem. He might have Supernatural to thank for that, as the actor explained:.

According to recent reports, every character is, for me, its own kind of entity. You know, I mean, even on Supernatural, I played 20 different versions of Sam, including playing Jared Paddleleki, you know? So I had some experience bouncing around between different versions of whatever my face looks like. But I enjoyed it, actually.

I would imagine that going from playing a wild superhero in maybe the crudest show on TV to working on a Christmas movie that’s made for families would be very fun. You’d get the best of both worlds in a lot of ways, and while whiplash may have been involved, jumping from one production to the other was great for Padalecki.

He also told me that Guarding Stars, which is a project on the 2026 movie schedule that sees him play an actor opposite Leighton Meester’s bodyguard as they decide they need to fake date, served as a nice palate cleanser, or shower, if you will:.

After finishing an episode of The Boys, you really want to take a shower and, like, get rid of it, especially the way you know my character ended in The Boys, literally. But this movie was feel-good. You went there, and you're like, ‘I'm gonna watch this with my kids and grandparents or whatever.’.

Recent findings suggest that I mean, Jared Padalecki did, as he noted, literally have to take a shower after The Boys; he was covered in so much blood after all was said and done. Going to do a Christmas movie afterward helped metaphorically cleanse him too.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

As I mentioned, in Guarding Stars, Padalecki plays an actor, Jack, who has to work with a bodyguard, who is played by Leighton Meester. They decide to fake date in an effort to keep her cover, and obviously, as these rom-coms go, cute shenanigans ensue, wholesome family moments happen, and real romantic feelings develop. It’s adorable!

Now, "adorable" is not an adjective you’d use to describe The Boys, so I can see why Jared Padalecki thought it was “weird” to jump between the two projects.

Now, if you’d like to see him drenched in blood, you can stream The Boys on Amazon Prime. If you want to see him falling head over heels for his bodyguard, you can catch Guarding Stars on Netflix starting November 18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there's a lot of ways to make money fast in GTA 6, from robbing jewelry stores, pawn shops, and banks to boosting cars, winning races, and even mugging strangers. But some jobs are more lucrative than others, and sometimes the payoff of a major heist isn't worth the time, prep work, and violence it takes to complete them. If you need some cash fast and easy, here are some ideas that are mostly low risk, high reward. Heck, a couple of them aren't even illegal!

Here's the best bit of advice you're going to get for making money in GTA 6: steal from your fellow thieves.

As you're out and about in the world, you'll often see a crime in progress: a bank robbery taking place, a jewelry store heist happening, an armored car being jacked, a drug deal down at the docks, or sometimes just a speeding vehicle filled with criminals fleeing from pursuing cops.

In a recent development, hit those criminals. Hard and fast. And then take their shit. Especially in Chapter 2 and Chapter 3, another criminal's sack of bills or jewels or drugs is worth lots more than the take you'll get from hitting most robbery locations yourself. If you see crooks fleeing with duffel bags over their backs, drop 'em. (You can do it non-lethally if you like, but drop 'em.).

Recent findings suggest that then grab their bags and beat cheeks because the heat that was on them will quickly be on you. Some robbery crews will have multiple bags of goods, so best to travel as a couple, Lucia and Jason, if only to be able to carry off all that re-stolen loot and cash it in with a fence. You don't want to leave a sack of cash or jewelry behind, right? And if you act quickly enough, you'll be able to make a clean getaway.

When you're out exploring Leonida, keep your ears open at all times. Hear sirens? Alarms? Gunshots? Screams? Cars speeding or crashing? Don't hesitate. Take out the other crew and grab the loot for yourself. It's usually a great payday.

It has been revealed that okay, a pretty obvious one, but once you hit Chapter 2 and meet a mechanic, Moses, who gives you a slim jim and will buy stolen cars, it's probably the best way to turn a quick profit for relatively little risk. A decent car (Moses is looking for older model, low profile cars) will usually net you between one and a few thousand dollars, which is better than most smash-and-grab jobs you'll be doing at that stage and way easier to pull off. This is because Moses pays well and the fence you have in Chapter 2 does not.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, the only drawback to Moses is that once he buys a stolen car, you can't sell him another for a bit. There's a significant plus, though: he will often tell you precisely where the cars he's looking for are located. Randy, your car fence starting in Chapter 3, will pay way more because he's after higher end, much flashier cars.

There are lots of races with nice payouts in GTA 6, but what if, like me, you're a terrible driver? The demolition races at Ambrosia Raceway are just the thing for those of you who tend to crash a lot anyway. Win on the oval track and you'll make over three grand, and it's double the take on the figure-eight track. Plus, you can repeat the races as many times as you like. Easy money.

In a recent development, the secret is, you come in first by default when all the other cars have been destroyed. If you can't beat 'em, just ram 'em, flip 'em, and destroy 'em. You don't even need to use your own wheels, just rent one from the track for a few hundred, spend a couple minutes slamming your front fender into everyone you see, and pocket the winnings long before you've done the eight laps.

The hunting payouts aren't huge at first, but as you start taking on hunting missions for your old military buddy Bret in Lummox County in Chapter 2 (these missions are for Jason only), he'll request you hunt creatures that he'll pay more and more for. Like Red Dead Redemption 2, there are legendary animals in GTA 6, and that means money.

You can take down the animals from Bret's lists or just find your own prey out in the world. Just today I was exploring, spotted a large boar in the woods, grabbed my rifle from my truck, and shot it: Bret paid me $2,500 and even came to pick up the carcass himself, saving me a trip. For smaller trophies, just park outside and step into Bret's building, and he'll auto-buy the dead critters right out of your trunk. Good deal.

According to recent reports, your entire criminal strategy will change in Chapter 3 when you get a tool called the snap gun. This lets you pick door locks, which means bypassing alarms. From then on, make sure the places you want to rob have a back door: it's the key to turning a quick smash-and-grab into a proper heist.

Coming in the back of the store is the way to do crime: you get inside without anyone (usually) immediately noticing, can quickly and quietly subdue any security or employees hanging around in the rear of the store, get quick access to the security footage (destroy it) and the alarm system (disable it) and can locate the safe before anyone knows a heist is going down.

With alarms off and your partner doing crowd control, you can take the time to make sure you're getting every penny out of the place. Smash every jewelry display case. Threaten someone for the safe code or find it written down somewhere in the office. Empty all the cash drawers, even take people's wallets and the drugs from first-aid kits. Do it right and you can make a clean getaway, avoiding the police pursuit altogether. Beautiful.

You'll meet a pilot in Chapter 3 and he'll start offering you regular work in Chapter 4. Get in your flying practice, though: these are time-sensitive jobs.

Pete will direct you to his plane and you'll use it to distribute cocaine around Leonida by dropping packages to buyers waiting below. You'll have multiple targets to hit across the map, and a time-limit: those buyers won't hang around forever, waiting. (I guess they have something more vital to do than acquiring huge bricks of coke?) Fly smart and plot your route efficiently and you'll make a nice chunk of change from each run.

There are, naturally, lots of other ways to make money, but most come with more risk, more time, or less of a haul.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss.
  • You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon.
  • As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Major Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

In a recent development, A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

In a recent development, peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has revealed he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the organization.
  • It has been revealed that in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the Board." 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has revealed he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the organization. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

It has been revealed that in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester noted of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My initiative was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the manufacturer's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

Wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the manufacturer in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox declared a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

It has been revealed that wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a new studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go.
  • As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts.
  • "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Newly introduced features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to recent reports, according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

Sources indicate that for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.
  • FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server concern".
  • FromSoftware never specified the exact problem impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server concern". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

FromSoftware never specified the exact problem impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

Industry observers note that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

Yes, I personally think GTA 6's Ultimate Edition is worth it, but it really depends how excited you are for the game and whether you want to get the most out of it.
